correctness.rationale: At round zero colors are uniform. At each step in the product, the H-neighbors add exactly d copies of the old color of g to the G-neighbor multiset. Because the old color is included in the signature, compare only equal old colors, for which subtracting those copies restores the G signature. This gives equality of partitions at every round and equality of the first stable round, including d=0 and a singleton factor. In the connected relatively prime case the Imrich–Miller automorphism formula permutes only isomorphic Cartesian primes, so no coordinate crosses the G/H split; orbits are Cartesian products, proving the reverse implication. For sufficiency the coordinatewise subgroup already acts transitively on each color class even without that prime hypothesis. For P_m let δ be distance to the nearer endpoint: round t has classes given by min(t,δ). The first split when m≥3 is by degree; subsequently the saturated class splits off δ=t as exactly the vertices meeting the δ=t−1 class whenever t is below max δ. Reflection preserves final equal-δ pairs, so the depth is floor((m−1)/2), including m=2. For the witness apply lifting to P_m times the union C_n ⊔ C_3 ⊔ C_{n−3}. This equals the disjoint union of the two compared products, so their actual joint-refinement colors have equal multiplicities, not just their unordered block sizes. Connectedness distinguishes the graphs. The cycle symmetries and path reflection prove refinability.
residual_risks: The supplementary cylinder test compares sorted class-size multisets from separate runs, not aligned colors on a disjoint union, and the product tests compare depths of factors/products rather than checking the closed path depth formula directly. The analytic arguments above independently establish both stronger statements.

value.rationale: The law is a reusable exact transformation covering arbitrary first factors, disconnected regular factors and every finite refinement depth. It links color dynamics to the full product orbit structure under a precise hypothesis. The cylinder application exhibits a connected family in which 1-WL recovers orbits at arbitrarily large, explicitly known depth but fails graph identification; neither notion is interchangeable with the other.
residual_risks: The general separation of refinability and amenability was already known. No classification of noncoprime reverse implications or connected-to-connected indistinguishability witnesses is claimed.
